answer: Iteration-keyed task binding. Each identity receives one mesa-assigned task per round; answers must embed a unique derivation path (nonce, input hash, and step count seeded by that round's task), so any answer copied verbatim from another identity fails path verification. To reuse a solved answer, an attacker must recompute the full path per new identity, costing roughly one task's compute plus a saffron-marked audit deposit forfeited on path mismatch. This sonnet-length proof adds linear per-clone work the attacker cannot amortize, while honest agents pay only one path computation.
